questions.q: What is the official term for the person or entity that orders the project for execution?
questions.n: The Owner is the primary stakeholder who commissions the project and enters into agreements with the architect and contractor.

questions.q: Who is the professional commissioned by the Owner, acting personally or through authorized assistants, to design and oversee the project?
questions.n: The Architect is the lead professional responsible for the creative design and technical supervision of the architectural works.

questions.q: Who is the person named in the Contract Documents or their authorized representative for technical engineering matters?
questions.n: The Engineer is the professional responsible for the structural, electrical, or mechanical engineering components as specified in the contract.

questions.q: Which term describes the full-time construction inspector hired by the Owner to assist the Architect and Engineer in overseeing the site?
questions.n: The Project Representative provides full-time inspection to ensure the work matches the drawings and specifications.

questions.q: The person or firm whose proposal was accepted and who has been awarded the Contract is known as the:
questions.n: The Contractor is the entity responsible for executing the construction work in exchange for the contract sum.

questions.q: What is the term for a firm with a direct contract with the Contractor to perform a specific portion of the work, excluding those who only provide materials?
questions.n: Sub-contractors deal directly with the main Contractor to complete specialized tasks like plumbing or electrical work.

questions.q: Which entity provides the guarantee for the Contractor’s Bonds?
questions.n: The Surety is the firm or corporation that guarantees the performance of the contractor's obligations to the owner.

questions.q: The offer of a Bidder to perform work, submitted on a prescribed form, is called a:
questions.n: A Proposal (or Bid) is the formal document where a bidder states their price and conditions for the project.

questions.q: What is the name of the cashier’s check or bond that guarantees the Bidder will enter into the Contract if their bid is awarded?
questions.n: The Proposal Bond protects the owner in case the winning bidder refuses to sign the contract.

questions.q: Which bond, usually 15% of the contract sum, is furnished before execution to guarantee the work will be done according to contract terms?
questions.n: A Performance Bond ensures that the project is completed by the contractor as specified in the contract.

questions.q: What bond is furnished to guarantee that the Contractor will pay all obligations (labor and materials) arising from the Contract?
questions.n: The Payment Bond protects the owner from liens by ensuring all workers and suppliers are paid by the contractor.

questions.q: Which 30% bond is given to guarantee the quality of materials, equipment, and workmanship for a specific period after project completion?
questions.n: A Guaranteed Bond covers defects in materials or workmanship that appear after the project is finished.

questions.q: What is the name of the formal contract between the Owner and Contractor, including all supplemental and general provisions?
questions.n: The Agreement is the foundational document that explicitly states the contract sum and signatures of the parties.

questions.q: What is the published notice that provides prospective bidders with the nature, date, and magnitude of a project?
questions.n: This document formally alerts the public or selected contractors that a project is available for bidding.

questions.q: What are the additional pieces of information issued to bidders before the date of bidding to clarify or modify the documents?
questions.n: A Bid Bulletin is the official method of providing clarifications or changes to all bidders simultaneously.

questions.q: Which document contains the list of rules on how to prepare bids and the conditions for the award?
questions.n: This document ensures all contractors follow the same format and rules during the bidding process.

questions.q: The graphical presentations of the work, including supplementary details and shop drawings, are collectively called:
questions.n: Drawings represent the visual and geometric instructions for the construction of the building.

questions.q: Which printed documents stipulate the procedural and administrative aspects of the contract?
questions.n: The General Conditions establish the rights, responsibilities, and relationships of the parties involved.

questions.q: What is the term for instructions issued prior to bidding that modify or supplement Drawings, Specifications, or General Conditions?
questions.n: Special Provisions address unique project requirements that are not covered in the standard documents.

questions.q: What are the written descriptions of work, material qualities, and modes of construction called?
questions.n: Specifications (Specs) provide the qualitative standards that the contractor must meet for every material and system.

questions.q: What is the term for additional information issued as an amendment specifically to the provisions of the Specifications?
questions.n: These add to or revise the existing specifications to tailor them to a specific project site or condition.

questions.q: What do you call an outline specification that lists the type or trade names of materials to be used?
questions.n: This table allows for a quick reference to ensure the correct colors, brands, and types of materials are used.

questions.q: Which document lists the work parts and indicates their corresponding values for materials, labor, profit, and overhead?
o: Breakdown of Work and Corresponding Value
questions.n: This is used for progress billing to determine how much the contractor should be paid based on work completed.

questions.q: Information delivered in person or via registered mail to the last known business address is legally termed:
questions.n: Written Notice is a requirement for many contractual actions, such as terminating a contract or claiming extra time.

questions.q: How do contracts refer to cataclysmic phenomena of nature, such as earthquakes or floods, that could not be foreseen?
o: Act of God or Force Majeure
questions.n: This clause excuses parties from liability for delays caused by uncontrollable natural events.

questions.q: The duration of time allowed by the Contract for the completion of the project is called:
questions.n: Time limits define the boundary of the project period; exceeding them can lead to liquidated damages.

questions.q: What is the collective term for all laws, ordinances, and governmental regulations applicable to the project?
questions.n: Contractors are obligated to follow all Local Laws, including the NBC, Fire Code, and zoning ordinances.

questions.q: Which term includes labor, materials, equipment, and transportation necessary to complete the construction?
questions.n: In a contract, 'The Work' represents everything the contractor must provide to achieve the final result.

questions.q: What is the contractual definition of the word 'Furnish'?
o: To purchase and/or fabricate and deliver to the jobsite
questions.n: Furnishing only covers getting the material to the site; it does not include putting it in place.

questions.q: What is the contractual definition of the word 'Install'?
o: To build in, mount, connect, or apply an object ready for intended use
questions.n: Installing focuses on the physical attachment and preparation of a furnished item for its final function.

questions.q: In construction documents, the word 'Provide' is understood to mean:
questions.n: If a spec says 'Provide a door', the contractor must both buy it/deliver it (furnish) and hang it (install).
